references.text: The leaders of Gilead seek a leader to fight against the Ammonites, which leads directly to Jephthah's call.
Jephthah accepts the role as chief and leader, and the negotiations are completed in Mizpah.
Moses appointed leaders (קָצִין) over the people; the same Hebrew word is used here for Jephthah's role.
Joshua appointed chiefs over the people, a similar leadership role to what Jephthah was asked to take.
The people of Israel ask Samuel for a king who can lead them in war, similar to the request made to Jephthah.
Isaiah mentions קָצִין as a leadership position in society, the same title offered to Jephthah.
Deborah calls Barak to lead Israel in battle, parallel to the call given to Jephthah against the Ammonites.
The book of Hebrews mentions Jephthah among the heroes of faith who conquered kingdoms through faith.
